response.passage: Germs are tiny living organisms, like bacteria and viruses, that are invisible to the naked eye. They do not just live on dirty or smelly objects; they are present everywhere, even on surfaces that look perfectly clean. Because you cannot see them, your hands may carry germs even when they appear spotless. Washing your hands with plain soap and water is highly effective because soap molecules break down the oily layer on your skin that traps germs, allowing them to be rinsed away easily. Simply rinsing with water is not enough, as it cannot remove this oily layer. Furthermore, it is a common myth that you only catch a cold from cold weather or rain; in reality, colds are caused by viruses, not the temperature. When you are sick, covering your mouth prevents these germs from spreading to others, which is a practice everyone should follow, not just those who are currently ill. Finally, when a doctor prescribes antibiotics for a bacterial infection, you must finish the entire course. Stopping the medicine early just because you feel better allows the remaining bacteria to survive and potentially become stronger, making the infection harder to treat later.
response.summary: Germs are invisible organisms that exist even on clean-looking surfaces. Proper handwashing with soap and finishing prescribed antibiotics are essential habits to prevent the spread of illness and ensure effective treatment.
